audit_findings.title: Post-Biocare balance sheet is paired with pre-Biocare owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed scale is a $950 million acquisition and $600 million of new 4.90% notes, implying $29.4 million annual pretax interest
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge uses July 2026 post-acquisition cash and debt, while anchor OE is FY2025 and excludes Biocare earnings, incremental financing cost and post-close acquisition effects.
audit_findings.evidence: As of October 31, 2025, we had approximately $3.4 billion in outstanding indebtedness which included an aggregate outstanding principal amount of $3.3 billion in unsecured senior notes.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated because the acquisition closed before the valuation date and the July 2026 filing includes Biocare from June 24. Direction is mixed: omitted Biocare earnings understate value, while omitted incremental interest and recurring integration costs overstate it. The transaction and financing are large enough relative to $1,250.7 million of anchor OE to require a rerun, although the net valuation effect is unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE through July 2026, isolate Biocare's filed post-close contribution, annualize it using supporting operating data, include $29.4 million of annual note interest plus integration and purchase-accounting effects, and rerun with numerator and bridge on the same perimeter.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 taxes are not a sustainable terminal baseline
audit_findings.magnitude: $85 million of disclosed FY2025 discrete tax benefits, equal to 6.8% of anchor OE; $102 million FY2025 Singapore tax-holiday benefit expires after 2030; FY2026 nine-month effective tax rate was 17.3% versus 9.2% in FY2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Unsustainable tax benefits can inflate anchor OE and all projected OE, with an especially large effect on terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our income taxes to increase in fiscal year 2026 due to top-up taxes under Pillar Two along with the implementation of the OBBBA rules.
audit_findings.explanation: The low FY2025 tax rate and subsequent increase are demonstrated. Whether the OE construction already removed every discrete benefit is unresolved, but the $85 million of discrete benefits alone is large enough to affect value materially, while the $102 million tax-holiday benefit cannot be carried unchanged beyond 2030.
audit_findings.action: Trace each FY2025 tax item through the $1,250.7 million OE calculation, remove any retained $57 million transfer benefit and $28 million reserve release, incorporate the filed FY2026 tax experience, and rerun terminal earnings at a documented post-2030 cash tax rate.

audit_findings.title: The failed liabilities parse leaves non-debt senior claims unaudited
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; July 2026 other long-term liabilities were $542 million, including $64 million of long-term tax liabilities, of which $41 million was top-up tax due within two years and $23 million related to uncertain tax positions
audit_findings.mechanism: A liability representing a past-period claim not captured by prospective OE should reduce the equity bridge; ordinary operating liabilities whose costs recur in OE should not be double-counted.
audit_findings.evidence: Other long-term liabilities as of October 31, 2025 and October 31, 2024 include $28 million and $115 million, respectively, related to long-term income tax liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The failed reconciliation is demonstrated, but the record does not establish that a material amount was omitted from the bridge. The specifically identified $64 million tax balance is only 0.33% of the $19.33 billion base equity value, while the composition and OE treatment of the remaining liabilities are unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile all $542 million of July 2026 other long-term liabilities and relevant current liabilities, including the $59 million of Biocare liabilities assumed, and classify each item as captured in prospective OE, offset by an asset, or requiring a separate bridge deduction; then rerun for confirmed omissions.

audit_findings.title: Serial acquisition spending may be recurring reinvestment excluded from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $862 million of acquisition cash outflow in FY2024 and $950 million in the first nine months of FY2026, equal to 68.9% and 76.0% of $1,250.7 million anchor OE, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: If acquisitions are required to sustain the earnings base or projected growth, a normalized acquisition or replacement-capital charge belongs in OE, particularly when acquired-intangible amortization is added back.
audit_findings.evidence: In the normal course of business, we frequently engage in discussions with third parties relating to possible acquisitions, strategic investments and alliances, joint ventures and divestitures, and generally expect to complete several transactions per year.
audit_findings.explanation: Frequent acquisition activity and spending of material scale are demonstrated. Whether that spending is maintenance-like reinvestment or optional growth investment remains unresolved, but even a modest recurring portion could materially reduce distributable OE and the terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile at least five to ten years of acquisition spending, acquired revenue and profit contribution, disposals, and intangible-amortization addbacks; estimate the portion required to maintain the earnings base and rerun OE with a documented normalized replacement-acquisition charge.

audit_findings.title: Growth may be credited without its required capital expenditure
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 capital expenditure was $407 million and the latest FY2026 forecast was $450 million, equal to 36.0% of anchor OE; the maintenance-versus-growth split is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Maintenance capital expenditure reduces anchor OE, while incremental capital expenditure and working capital needed for 3% to 6% growth reduce projected distributable OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Our anticipated capital expenditures for fiscal year 2026 will be approximately $500 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The sizable and rising capital program is demonstrated, including manufacturing-capacity expansion. The record does not show how much is maintenance capital or prove that scenario OE is after growth reinvestment, but the filed spending scale is plainly capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the capex deduction used in anchor OE to filed cash expenditures, separate maintenance from expansion spending, quantify working-capital needs, and rerun each growth scenario after the reinvestment required to support its growth rate.

audit_findings.title: The stated fully diluted share ceiling is not an actual ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: at most 2.040 million additional shares if the entire combined target inventory were performance awards, a 0.72% denominator increase and approximately $0.48 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: Performance awards settling above target increase fully diluted shares and reduce value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The final LTPP award may vary from zero to 200 percent of the target award.
audit_findings.explanation: The ceiling label is incorrect because LTPP awards can settle at 200% of target. However, even the conservative upper bound of doubling the entire 2.040 million combined RSU/LTPP inventory would increase the 284.882854 million-share denominator by only 0.72%, reducing the $67.85 base value by about $0.48 per share; the actual effect must be smaller because fixed RSUs are included in that inventory.
audit_findings.action: Separate fixed RSUs from LTPP awards and calculate the contractual 200% performance-share inventory; update the bull-case denominator and relabel the denominator as a ceiling only after that reconciliation.
